items.title: Global Economic Outlook & Strategy: A Tenuous Balance
items.summary: The global economy is still powering ahead even as uncertainties — from the sustainability of the AI boom to geopolitics — continue to mount. We see global growth coming in at 2.7% this year and climbing to 2.8% next year, as pressures from the U.S.-Iran conflict eventually moderate.

items.title: ECB: Three Pillars, But One Direction
items.summary: The ECB held rates steady, but communications brought apparently conflicting messages: signals of a December hike, especially if the inflation outlook is revised higher, alongside an implied higher bar for tightening policy. For now, we continue to expect a 25-basis-point hike in December.

items.title: Foreign Exchange Forecasts: October 2026
items.summary: We lower our 0-3m EURUSD forecast to 1.1050 as European tail risks remain unresolved; we expect rate differentials to move back in favor of USD; and the U.S.-Iran conflict continues to keep energy prices elevated. We keep our 6-12m EURUSD forecast at 1.13, for reasons explored herein.

items.title: Emerging Markets Strategy Weekly: Competing Crosscurrents
items.summary: Emerging markets continue to face competing macro crosscurrents, with oil, AI sentiment and the emerging El Niño cycle likely to remain key drivers of market direction. We see limited evidence that EI Niño risks are adequately priced, leaving EM assets vulnerable to a further repricing.

items.title: Four Takeaways From Semi/Semi-Equipment Earnings So Far
items.summary: SOX has retraced 8% since our earnings preview, consistent with our view that investors should become more selective as estimate revisions moderate. A third of the way through earnings season, we see four key developments emerging, which we explore in this note.

items.title: Off the Cuff: Clearing Hurdles
items.summary: The sprint to year's end is looking more like a 100-meter hurdles event. A third of the way through, the SPX is off to a solid start, though the more trying parts of the race are still ahead. That we are close to all-time highs is a storyline in and of itself given the hurdles to be leapt.

items.title: Microsoft's Acceleration Curve Steepens With Impressive Quarter
items.summary: Microsoft's strong results brought signs of AI tailwinds, with broad-based upside across Azure and strength in CoPilot/M365. The results show MSFT's core business is benefitting as enterprise customers increasingly move AI into production. We raise our estimates and our target price.

items.title: ServiceNow's AI Acceleration May Require More Patience
items.summary: ServiceNow delivered mixed results against more elevated expectations. While AI momentum was strong, the fourth-quarter outlook was mixed. While that's a more complicated picture, we think 2027 could see accelerated AI consumption usage. We lower our target price to $157 for Buy-rated NOW.

items.title: Oracle Offers Greater Clarity on AI Growth and Funding
items.summary: Oracle's Analyst Day left us increasingly confident that its AI strategy is strengthening from a demand and financing perspective. We reiterate our Buy rating and positive catalyst view and see room for recovery in shares, with demand staying strong and financing concerns likely to ease.

items.title: Is This the Bottom for Boston Scientific?
items.summary: Boston Scientific posted better-than-expected results on low expectations, but forward commentary was incrementally worse. Which leads us to ask if expectations have finally hit a bottom. It wasn’t a pretty quarter, but 2027 commentary seems to be hugging the bottom.

items.title: We're Upgrading WEG to Buy
items.summary: We're upgrading WEG to Buy given strong data-center demand. Analyzing recently disclosed data about potential compute buildout commitments, we estimate that up to $3.4 billion could be addressable for WEG equipment. We also lift our target price to R$54 from R$49.50.

items.title: The Speculative Grade Beat: Bonds Are Back
items.summary: We add some risk back into our recommendations, starting with our Asset Allocation Framework, in which we return to a 55%/45% weighting in favor of high-yield bonds. That's based on improving relative value, a steadier rates backdrop, and rebounding high-beta performance.

items.title: AI Investment Supports Strong U.S. Domestic Demand
items.summary: Real GDP rose a seasonally adjusted 3.4% quarter over quarter, with a very strong 4.9% increase in final private domestic demand. AI-related investment remains a substantial driver of growth, but much of this investment is not domestically produced, with surging imports weighing on growth.

items.title: UK Autumn Budget Offers Breathing Room ... for Now
items.summary: The chancellor delivered a UK autumn budget that was market-friendly, maintaining headroom against fiscal rules with an absence of negative surprises. But this was still a tax-raising budget, and all the key problems still remain. We offer further analysis in this note.

items.title: “Medicine Starting to Work Some” As Fed Holds Rates Steady
items.summary: Chair Warsh dovishly noted that higher policy rates are having their expected effect in tightening financial conditions and acknowledged rates may already be at appropriate settings. As we explore herein, we continue to think the U.S. economy's breadth of strength is being overstated.

items.title: European Equity Strategy: When Rotation Reaches Extremes
items.summary: European equities have seen one of the sharpest rotations on record, with Defensive outperformance vs. Cyclicals breaching a threshold only usually seen amid major market stress. But unlike in the past, the European index remains near highs. We look at what may lie ahead.

items.title: What’s in the Price for Data Centers?
items.summary: Stocks exposed to data centers have underperformed amid broader market concerns about financing the AI trade. Following the recent de-rating, we estimate that data-center growth peaking in 2027 and then reverting to single-digit growth is now in the price, which we see as overly negative.

items.title: Canada Raises Rates on Yet-to-Materialize Upside Inflation Risks
items.summary: Canada raised rates 25 basis points as markets had priced, contrary to our expectations. This was framed as “risk management,” with decisions to be made “carefully.” Officials are now heavily focused on headline inflation; a further rise in energy prices could mean another near-term hike.

items.title: Global Gas and Power Insights: Potential Outcomes for TTF
items.summary: Given a potential escalation of the Middle East conflict, we assess what the market could be pricing and a potential range of outcomes for TTF. As we explore herein, it appears increases in winter 2026-27, 2027 and 2028 strips are all pricing similar probabilities of escalation.

items.title: We're Upgrading MercadoLibre to Buy
items.summary: We're upgrading MercadoLibre to Buy as we believe recent share-price weakness creates an attractive entry point. Although our 2027-28 estimates remain below consensus, MELI continues to grow materially more quickly than local consumer markets regardless of the macro backdrop.

items.title: U.S. Biotechnology: Third-Quarter Preview
items.summary: Heading into third-quarter earnings, we outline expectations across our commercial SMID biotech names, with refreshed models for AGIO, RYTM and ROIV and notes about what we'll be watching for from the three.

items.title: Japan FX: Checkpoints for the USDJPY
items.summary: We expect the USDJPY to remain in the range of ¥155/$ to ¥160/$ near term, but see the risk associated with the U.S. midterms as marginally to the upside. We believe the next round of intervention to buy the JPY will be when the pair reaches around ¥160/$, with further analysis herein.

items.title: Australia Economics: Hot CPI Print All But Confirms a Rate Hike
items.summary: Australia's third-quarter trimmed-mean inflation rose 1.0% quarter over quarter, all but confirming a 25-basis-point hike in November. The data validate our thesis of second-half price re-acceleration driven by too-strong domestic demand and ongoing supply shocks.

items.title: China’s Silver Economy, Pt. 3: Retiring Wealthier, Aging Better
items.summary: After decades of wealth accumulation, many in China are entering retirement with the means and the willingness to invest in their quality of life. We see this trend at the heart of China's silver economy, creating opportunities across elderly care, active lifestyles, and preventive health.

items.title: The High-Grade Beat: Hyperscalers Test New Wides
items.summary: Hyperscaler spreads have reached their widest levels since the AI funding wave began in U.S. investment grade last year, as investors keep demanding a premium for the uncertainty around further supply. But a supply-driven decompression has its limits, with implications we explore herein.

items.title: Global Commodities: Geopolitics, Energy and Weather Converge
items.summary: Agricultural markets remain supported by a rare convergence of risks, including geopolitical disruptions, high fertilizer and diesel costs, resilient biofuel demand, and the potential for a strong El Niño. We believe markets continue to underestimate the vulnerability of global balances.

items.title: Inflation Weekly: Let’s Talk About the PCE-CPI Wedge
items.summary: Core CPI inflation typically runs slightly stronger than core PCE inflation, but that's reversed this year. Much of the stickiness in PCE is concentrated in goods and services consumers aren't necessarily paying for directly, a dynamic that could further complicate monetary policy.

items.title: How to Navigate Brazil's Tougher Market Reality
items.summary: Brazil’s leftward shift caught markets by surprise, with investors now adjusting. Amid mounting macro-to-micro uncertainties, we screen our coverage into three buckets, aimed at helping investors navigate Brazil's new reality: stories to avoid, places to hide, and flight-to-quality names.

items.title: Africa Weekly: The Egyptian Pound Under Pressure
items.summary: A de-escalation of the Middle East conflict could support the Egyptian pound into year's end. But the current pressure highlights the difficult short-term policy choices facing the Central Bank of Egypt. We also look at Cote d’Ivoire's longer-term policy choices and their implications.

items.title: We're Upgrading Ferguson Enterprises to Buy
items.summary: We're upgrading Ferguson Enterprises to Buy with a $288 target price following recent share-price weakness, with our positive view based on the acquisition of FloWorks, large capital-project share gains, and more resilient residential exposure.  We offer further analysis in this note.

items.title: Equity Markets Positioning Model: Short Activity in Ascendence
items.summary: Global activity was bearish across the board after the recent rotation into Europe. We saw de-risking across equity indices driven largely by the initiation of new short positions. Nasdaq and S&P 500 positioning reduced further but already bearish Russell 2000 activity was more muted.

items.title: What's Next for EU–China Trade?
items.summary: Will the recent EU-China hybrid-vehicle deal pave the way for a meaningful rebalancing of trade between the two powers, or risk escalation that could spiral into a full-blown trade war? We assess the state of EU-China trade relations and consider potential scenarios in this note.

items.title: Brazil Equity Strategy: What Lula's Win Means for Markets
items.summary: We expect Lula’s victory to be seen negatively by the market, as it surprised investors and reinforces the downside asymmetry highlighted in our pre-election survey. Investors' concerns include fiscal policy, state-owned enterprises and the broader reform agenda.

items.title: Verizon's Results Point to Transformation Progress
items.summary: Verizon reported generally solid third-quarter results with better profitability as overall revenue missed, largely on lower equipment revenue. Guidance was lifted across major line items, reflecting that the upside will largely boost the CY26 outlook. We offer further analysis herein.

items.title: Changing ECB Communications, Changing Times
items.summary: An apparent change of emphasis in ECB communications from its first pillar (inflation outlook) to the other two (underlying inflation dynamics and policy transmission) justifies market expectations for a more moderate path. We take a deeper look at what's changed and what may lie ahead.

items.title: Mexico Economics: Data Point to a Firmer Footing
items.summary: Mexico's economic activity surprised to the upside in the third quarter, leading us to raise our 2026 GDP growth forecast to 1.9%.  Recent data suggest the economy entered the second half of the year with stronger momentum than expected. We look at potential tailwinds in this note.

items.title: U.S. Economics Weekly: Markets Contemplate an AI Slowdown
items.summary: U.S. (and global) economic growth has become increasingly dependent on the AI buildout. Markets have begun to see an AI spending slowdown as increasingly likely, leading to lower equity prices, wider credit spreads, and lower Treasury yields. We also look at scenarios for the Fed herein.

items.title: Global Macro Strategy: Tasting Notes for Risk-Off: Hints of AI, France, or Energy?
items.summary: Risk-off sentiment is emerging across asset classes as markets contend with AI financing concerns, French fiscal risks and high energy prices. We assess which themes are driving markets most, examine credit and equity signals, and discuss hedging opportunities across rates, FX and Europe.

items.title: Japan Equity Strategy in a "Bad Rate Decline" Phase
items.summary: The correction in Japanese equities reflects a phase where long-term rates and share prices are falling together as investors price in economic risks. We view this as a temporary risk-off episode and see scope for a rebound in equities, including a return to high-quality growth names.

items.title: U.S. Rates Weekly: Sentiment Shift
items.summary: Treasuries are showing signs of regaining their safe-haven role, while market sentiment has turned more constructive. We continue to expect the 5-year sector to outperform in further rate rallies and discuss positioning opportunities tied to a bull-flattening move.

items.title: Metal Matters: LME Week Recap
items.summary: LME Week participants expressed a cautious 2027 outlook for industrial metals amid weak growth, AI risks, energy prices and other concerns, although long-term structural and strategic upside optimism persists. We're cautious metals on geopolitical risks ahead of Israeli and U.S. elections.

items.title: BP's Substantial Discount Offers Opportunity
items.summary: Ahead of 3Q reporting, we reiterate the valuation case for bp. We estimate the stock trades at a 25% discount to Shell, 30% to European peers and 50% to U.S. peers. We think the market is underappreciating stronger operating performance, and another solid quarter could shift sentiment.

items.title: U.S. Telecom Infrastructure: SpaceX to Build a National Wireless Network?
items.summary: Bloomberg reports SpaceX is in talks to access at least 80,000 U.S. cell sites as it pursues a fourth nationwide wireless network. We see a mobile build scenario as positive for tower stocks and remain Buyers of CCI, SBAC, AMT and ECHO.

items.title: U.S. Engineering & Construction: 3Q26 Preview
items.summary: Despite noise around AI and infrastructure investment, we believe robust backlogs and company-specific execution should support results. Industry discussions still indicate demand exceeds supply. PWR remains our top pick; we also see upside in MTZ, FLR and J.

items.title: PULSE Monitor: Confidence Problem
items.summary: Confidence was shaken as markets grappled with the debt and equity issuance needed to finance datacenter buildouts. Investors have punished both spenders and beneficiaries, driving a flight to safety. Next week's Hyperscaler results could help stabilize sentiment if cloud growth holds up.

items.title: Citi 2026 Quant Conference Recap
items.summary: At Citi’s Quant Conference, speakers discussed AI in markets, capital flows and portfolio construction. AI is emerging as an asset-pricing variable and reshaping workflows, while crowding, risk models, optimization sensitivity and data quality remain key investment considerations.

items.title: Global Equities: AI Skepticism Trims Tech Crowding, Defensives and Energy Outperform
items.summary: Skepticism around the AI capex cycle reduced Technology crowding, though Growth crowding remains elevated. During the market pullback, crowded sectors lagged while uncrowded Consumer Staples and Health Care outperformed. Energy was a notable exception, posting strong gains.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence: Chaperoning Intelligence
items.summary: As AI turns decade-old PHP flaws into working exploits affecting software that powers 70% of websites, security spending may shift toward frontier models and agentic tools. Power-efficient inference and agent security may be key signals at Oracle AI World and ODSC AI West next week.

items.title: Oil Monitor: Near-Term Upside Risks and Global Marketing Takeaways
items.summary: Near-term oil risks remain skewed to the upside despite recovering Arab Gulf flows, with freight dislocations due to logistical inefficiencies preventing a full normalization of delivered supply. Geopolitical risks could re-emerge around Israeli legislative and U.S. mid-term elections.

items.title: European Rates Weekly: L’éléphant in the Room
items.summary: The ECB may find it difficult to avoid France as EGB spread volatility increasingly influences policy. We also examine UK curve steepeners that have limited exposure to front-end selloffs, and assess the underperformance and liquidity challenges of French SSAs.

items.title: Mexico Economics Weekly: A Weak FX Won’t Help Much
items.summary: Banxico has signaled it will not follow Fed hikes mechanically, contributing to peso weakness. We see limited economic benefit from a weaker currency, though financial stability risks could rise. Our base case is for stable rates, despite a bias toward cuts.
